title: Layout-flow benchmark task (klt.design_agent_benchmark.layout_task/1)
description: One task of the layout-flow benchmark (epic #2252): a frozen schematic netlist + spec -- never a layout -- plus the repo-frozen artifacts that make the task eligible under layout-protocol.json's `task_eligibility` rules. Extends task.schema.json rather than forking it: `block_spec` is that schema's own definition. The phase-2 corpus (#3025) keeps each task, with its frozen files, under `layout-corpus/<id>/task.json`; pass/fail for a *run* is never defined here -- it is the protocol's frozen validity gate.

repoPath.description: Repository-relative path; absolute paths and '..' segments are rejected by the validator.

id.description: Stable slug; must match the task's filename stem.

frozen_netlist.description: The schematic netlist LVS compares against. Frozen: the scorer reads this, never an agent-supplied copy.

reference_layout.description: Repo-frozen layout that is DRC-clean and LVS-clean against `frozen_netlist` (eligibility rule `reference_layout_valid`). Never shown to an agent.

generator_recipe.description: A `klt gen`/`klt gen-compose` request that reaches a valid layout (eligibility rule `generator_reachable`). Proves the gen-only arm satisfiable; never shown to an agent.

negative_controls.description: Known-bad layouts the validity gate must reject (eligibility rule `negative_controls`).

agent_inputs.description: Repo paths a candidate agent may be shown (phase 2, #3025): the frozen netlist and nothing else. The reference layout, generator recipe and negative controls are scorer-only; the corpus gate rejects a descriptor whose agent inputs contain any of them or any layout stream, so no scored candidate layout ships with a task.

eligibility.description: Why the task is eligible for all three arms (#3025): one evidence line per protocol `task_eligibility` rule id, and one per arm. A task failing any rule is listed in the corpus exclusions document instead, never scored on fewer arms.
